sections.html:
One combined notice arrives each year from the county tax collector, built on values the property appraiser set. Charlotte County collects in arrears, so a November bill pays for the calendar year that is nearly over.

The notice has two kinds of charge. Ad valorem tax follows value. Non-ad valorem assessments follow things like square footage or the number of units, and the collector names stormwater, fire and rescue and solid waste as examples. County commissioners, the School Board, city commissioners and other authorities set millage, and the appraiser does not.

The county had about 217,212 residents in 2025, and 83.8% of its 131,960 housing units have owner occupants. Median home value is $328,900. Because 87.3% of residents stayed put over the past year, many carry capped assessments, while a buyer starts from the reset value.

Each office has its own lane: the appraiser sets value and approves exemptions, the collector issues and takes payment on the bill, and the clerk runs tax deed sales.

  • Property appraiser: values, exemptions and homestead applications, phone (941) 743-1593 for exemption questions on a notice and (941) 743-1498 for assessed value questions.
  • Tax collector: bills, discounts, installment plans and delinquent taxes, phone (941) 743-1350.
  • Clerk's office: online tax deed sales, phone (941) 637-2130.

Installment applications go by mail to the collector at 18500 Murdock Circle, Port Charlotte, FL 33948. If you sold the house, send any bill that reaches you on to the buyer or return it to the collector.

Statements go out by the first of November, and paying early earns a sliding discount that starts at 4% and shrinks one point a month.

Charlotte County billing and collection steps
StepTiming or amount
Statements mailedBy November 1
Early paymentFour points off in the first month, then one fewer each month through February
DelinquentApril 1, with 3% interest plus advertising costs
Installment eligibilityEstimated tax over $100
Installment paymentsJune 30 (6% off), September 30 (4.5%), December 31 (3%), March 31 (none)
Certificate saleBy June 1, bidding down from 18%

When an escrow account pays the tax, the mortgage company should request the bill and the owner gets a copy for information.

Send the application to the collector before May 1. The first payment is due by June 30.

Skip the first payment and the plan is cancelled, which leaves the whole tax due by March 31. Once you make that payment, you are in for the year and enrollment renews on its own. To leave, ignore the June bill and wait for the November notice at the gross amount. Anything unpaid on April 1 is treated as a delinquent bill.

Installments one and two are each a quarter of the estimate. Numbers three and four add half of any true-up each, so the last two bills can differ from the first two.

Real estate tax left unpaid turns delinquent April 1 and heads to a certificate sale by early June.

The collector advertises delinquent parcels in a local paper weekly for three weeks, and advertising and collection fees land on the delinquent account. The sale is a reverse auction on the interest rate starting at 18%, and the lowest bidder gets the certificate, a first lien. A certificate is valid for seven years. Two years after the delinquency date, the holder can seek a tax deed, and the clerk conducts the sale online.

  • Delinquent taxes are accepted only by cashier's check, money order or cash.
  • A deed sale opens at a total that includes a $75.00 collector fee, a $150.00 ownership and encumbrance report, a $60.00 clerk fee and a $59.00 web fee, plus taxes, interest and half the assessed value.
  • Paying all taxes, costs and interest before the deed is issued stops the sale.

The county appraiser takes homestead applications until March 1 of the year you want the benefit, and you must live there as a permanent resident by New Year's Day.

State law gives up to $50,000 off. School taxes see only the first $25,000, while the added $25,000 applies on value above $50,000, for non-school levies. Later growth in assessed value is capped at 3 percent or CPI, and the state's chart prints a 2.7 percent cap for 2026. Selling resets the figure to full just value the following January 1.

Renting the home out ends homestead, except for the servicemember rule in the statutes. Seniors and veterans may qualify for extra benefits, and the appraiser's office rules on each case.

The collector also bills tangible personal property tax, which falls on the furniture and equipment of a business or rental property and on structural additions to mobile homes. These bills go out with the real estate bills and earn the same early discounts.

On April 1 tangible tax goes delinquent and picks up 1.5% interest, a $2.00 late fee and advertising costs. Warrants are issued before April 30 on unpaid accounts, and within 30 days the office applies to the circuit court for an order allowing levy and seizure.

  • Redeeming a certificate on or after June 1 adds a $6.25 redemption fee.
  • Paper bills can be swapped for email bills through the office's Bill Express sign-up, though an undeliverable bill doesn't extend a discount period.
  • Email addresses given for e-billing become public records.

Your closing agent divides the year's tax between the two parties and takes anything owed, delinquent amounts included, out of the proceeds.

Call (941) 743-1350 for a payoff and ask whether a certificate was sold, since a holder has to be repaid with interest before the lien clears. The deed carries the state's 70 cents per $100 stamp tax, paid at recording, with every party to the document liable.

A buyer of a homesteaded house won't inherit the seller's exemption or capped value. Ask both offices for figures on your parcel.

Request a written payoff from the collector before you accept an offer. Hand a copy to the title agent and, if you owe back taxes, ask how the certificate holder gets repaid. Check that any installment plan is settled or assigned in the contract. After closing, keep the settlement statement and the paid receipt. A cash sale skips the lender's underwriting, but the tax payoff is the same step either way.

faqs.q: Which office mails the Charlotte County bill?
faqs.a: The Charlotte County Tax Collector mails it on or before November 1, using the roll certified by the property appraiser. Call (941) 743-1350 with billing questions.

faqs.q: What is the early payment discount in Charlotte County?
faqs.a: Four percent off in November, falling one point each month to 1% in February. March brings none, and delinquency starts April 1.

faqs.q: Can Charlotte County taxes be paid in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, when the estimate exceeds $100 and the application is in before May 1. Four payments follow, ending March 31.

faqs.q: When can a tax certificate turn into a tax deed application?
faqs.a: Two years after the tax went delinquent. A certificate lasts seven years, and redemption is possible until a deed is issued.

faqs.q: Where do I file for homestead in Charlotte County?
faqs.a: Send it to the county appraiser by March 1. That office decides eligibility, and the collector only bills.
